source.snippet: Do think about b2b. Companies are already paying much more for AI. A new K3 (or similar model) every 6 months for a monthly rate of ~100$ per month is something MANY businesses would pay for. Then they could even sell them at half the price to consumers.

problem_statement: Businesses paying for AI inference at scale face unpredictable cost and performance cliffs as models rapidly iterate every 6 months, with no good mechanism to lock in performance SLAs or cost predictability across model generations.
target_segment: B2B SaaS companies and AI-heavy startups that budget $100–$1000/month on AI API costs and need cost/performance stability.
notes: Commenter explicitly references businesses paying 'much more' for AI and a $100/month price point many businesses would accept. AMD/Taalas acquisition context implies hardware-level cost compression is coming, which creates arbitrage opportunity for AI cost management or model-version hedging services.
